diagnosis_explanation:
Your neck has some pain. This pain also goes down your right arm. This is called radiculopathy.

You have a problem in your neck bones. It is called cervical spondylosis. This makes it hard for your spinal cord to move. There is also a soft cushion between your neck bones. It has slipped out a little. This is called a herniated nucleus pulposus. It presses on nerves in your neck. This causes your arm pain.

This has made the space in your neck bones smaller. This is called stenosis. It can cause pain and numbness.
medication_rationale:
Decadron - stopping:
Your doctor wants you to stop taking this medicine. You were treated with this medicine for your neck pain. Do not take it until your doctor tells you it is safe to start again.

Medrol:
This medicine is a steroid. It helps reduce swelling in your body. This swelling can cause pain and pressure. You may notice some mood changes. You might feel more awake or have trouble sleeping. This is often normal. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing or feel very weak. Also call if you get a fever or chills.

Darvocet:
This medicine is for pain. It will help ease your neck pain. You might feel sleepy or dizzy. This is common when you start. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing. Also call if you feel very confused.

Flexeril:
This medicine helps relax your muscles. It can ease muscle tightness. This tightness may be part of your neck pain. You may feel drowsy or dizzy. This medicine can make you feel sleepy. Call your doctor if you feel very tired. Also call if your heart beats very fast.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel tired and sore after surgery.
- Pain in your neck and arm may be worse at first.
- Wear your neck brace as instructed.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- You cannot drive a car this week.
- Eat soft foods that are easy to chew.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble swallowing.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 5 minutes twice a day.

**Week 2:**
- Your neck and arm pain may start to get a little better.
- You might feel more energy than last week.
- Continue to wear your neck brace.
- Keep lifting no more than 5 pounds.
- You still cannot drive a car.
- You can eat a wider range of soft foods.
- Call your doctor if your pain gets much worse.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes twice a day.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel less pain and more comfort.
- You can start to do light chores around the house.
- Continue to wear your neck brace as directed.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- You may be able to drive short distances if cleared by your doctor.
- You can eat most normal foods now.
- Call your doctor if you notice any redness or swelling at your incision.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 15 minutes twice a day.

**Week 4:**
- Your energy levels should continue to improve.
- You can do more normal daily activities.
- Ask your doctor about removing your neck brace.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 15 pounds.
- You can likely drive as usual if you feel ready.
- You can return to your normal diet.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worsening arm weakness.
- Your goal this week is to walk outside for 20 minutes once a day.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel steady progress each week.
- Neck and arm pain will gradually decrease.
- Keep following activity limits until your doctor says otherwise.
- Healing takes time, so be patient with yourself.
- Most people return to normal activities within 6 to 12 weeks.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Neck pain is sudden and severe: This could be a spinal bleed.
- You cannot move your arms or legs: This is a spinal cord emergency.
- You lose bladder or bowel control: This needs urgent medical care.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Your pain gets much worse: Medicine may not be enough now.
- You have numbness or tingling: These signals may be blocked.
- You feel new weakness in your arm: Your nerves may be squeezed.
- Your arm or hand swells badly: This could block blood flow.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Neck pain slowly gets better: This is a normal healing sign.
- You have mild arm pain: This can happen as you heal.
- Numbness or tingling is mild: This may improve over time.
- You have questions about your medicine: Your doctor can help you.
